what_it_does: Modern data centers need to send data between GPUs and servers at extremely high speeds using wired connections, but long cables lose signal strength—the signal gets 52 decibels weaker over the distance. This paper designs a receiver chip that recovers that degraded signal accurately, using a clever filtering trick. Instead of bulky and power-hungry coils in the receiver's input stage, the team uses a clever resonant (LC) circuit arrangement to amplify the right frequencies and suppress noise. The whole chip is built in ultra-dense 4-nanometer transistors, making it efficient enough for data-center deployment.
